subject: Draft MAP & licensing proposal for Private/VPC deployment — Industrial.ai
messages:
From: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@industrial.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@industrial.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP request — Private deployment evaluation

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, we need a mutual action plan (MAP) that ties evaluation milestones to procurement and licensing milestones for our Private/VPC deployment. Key asks from my side:

- A clear list of evaluation milestones (POC, scale run, security review) and expected timelines (weeks relative to start).
- Commercial triggers: when do commitments/committed capacity and platform fees kick in? Any ramp discounts?
- A concise licensing summary for on-prem/VPC (platform fee, per-GPU vs per-seat, support tiers).
- Attachables for procurement: SOC 2 evidence, SOW template, draft license.

Can you send a draft MAP and a high-level commercial proposal by next Wednesday (Mar 11)? Procurement will want the items lined up for their internal review.

Cheers,
Alice Barnes
Director, Cloud Platform
Industrial.ai

[Attachment: RFI_SecurityChecklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@industrial.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP request — Draft MAP and commercial outline

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP and a licensing summary tailored to Private/VPC deployments. High level summary below so procurement can scan quickly:

MAP (high level)
- Week 0: Kickoff + access provisioning (Redwood provides staging VPC template + onboarding doc).
- Week 1–3: POC (functional validation, latency benchmarks, integration with Industrial.ai auth).
- Week 4–6: Scale run (throughput validation at agreed QPS; load testing).
- Week 7: Security & compliance review (SOC 2 evidence + KMS integration testing).
- Week 8–10: Production readiness and cutover plan; SOW finalization.

Commercial triggers and milestones
- Evaluation (Weeks 0–3): No platform fee; hosted trial capacity provided for POC (limited to 2 x A100-equivalents).
- Scale run (Weeks 4–6): Option to spin up dedicated capacity; estimated commit discussion starts at week 4.
- Commitment & Platform Fee: Platform fee begins on contract signature if Private deployment is selected; we can agree to a phased ramp where committed capacity billing starts 30 days after signature, with a 3-month ramp discount at 40% off list during months 1–3 of the commit.
- Discounts: 12-month commit -> additional 10% off platform fee; 24-month -> additional 18%.

Licensing summary (Private/VPC)
- Platform fee: annual base fee covering control plane, private deployment tooling, and long-term support (suggested: $125k annual for enterprise plan — draft).
- Capacity commitment: priced as committed GPU-hours per month (or reserved node pools). Example: 4 reserved A100-equivalent nodes = $X/month (see attached breakout).
- Support: Standard SLA included; Premium support (24x7 + named TAM) add-on.

Attachments included: IndustrialAI_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestone owner fields), RDW_Private_VPC_Licensing_Summary.pdf, SOW-draft-IndustrialAI.pdf

I'll be on a short trip next week but will respond quickly to procurement. Rishi — can you and Vivek review the ramp discount language and confirm the platform fee ranges before I send a more formal commercial?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: IndustrialAI_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Initial MAP request — need pricing sign-off (internal)

Team — forwarding Alice's MAP request and my draft. Quick notes:

- Alice asked explicitly when platform fee and capacity billing kick in relative to the MAP milestones. I proposed contract signature triggers platform fee, with billing for committed capacity delayed by 30 days and a 3-month 40% ramp discount.
- Procurement will push for platform fee waiver or deeper ramp discounts tied to early commits. They may try to move platform fee to go-live not contract.
- Risk: If we push platform fee start to go-live, we lose visibility for early customer ops costs; if they insist, we can offer a small credit or longer commit term.

Requested: Rishi, suggest a concession ladder we can use (waive platform fee for X months vs deeper commit discounts). Vivek, confirm technical feasibility of 30-day delay for committed nodes in private/VPC deployments and whether we can allow a 60-day delay if needed. Grace, prep SOC 2 artifact list and SSO/KMS onboarding checklist for procurement.

I plan to push back on a full platform fee waiver but willing to give 2 months waived or up to 50% off platform fee for the first quarter in exchange for a 12-month commit at the suggested capacity. Thoughts?

— Marissa

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@industrial.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@industrial.ai>
Cc: Industrial.ai Procurement <procurement@industrial.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and commercial outline — Procurement ask

Marissa,

Thanks — the MAP is very helpful. Procurement has two asks before they can greenlight the schedule:

1) Platform fee timing: They prefer platform fee to start at production cutover (go-live) rather than at contract signature. If Redwood needs earlier fees, they'd like a credit so net platform charge over the first 12 months is equal to starting at go-live.

2) Ramp economics: They want a structured ramp where we pay a modest committed capacity in month 1 (25% of target), then 50% month 2, 75% month 3, and 100% month 4 — with a 45% discount applied to the first three months compared to post-ramp committed pricing.

Procurement also asked for an approvable SOW and a short list of the exact control-plane features included in the platform fee (audit logs, routing, billing integration). Attached is their internal procurement template — they asked us to populate the commercial fields.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the ramp cadence and the discount structure? If not, please propose a counter that preserves our revenue visibility.

Regards,
Tom Ellis
VP, Infrastructure Engineering
Industrial.ai

[Attachment: IndustrialAI_ProcurementTemplate.docx (docx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@industrial.ai>, Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@industrial.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and commercial outline — Redwood counter and next steps

Tom and team — thanks for the clear procurement asks. We want to keep the MAP timeline intact; below is our counter-proposal intended to balance Industrial.ai's onboarding runway with Redwood's operational and commercial needs.

Redwood counter (high level)
- Platform fee timing: Move platform fee invoicing start to go-live, with a one-time non-refundable onboarding deposit equal to 25% of the annual platform fee due on signature. That deposit will be credited against the first invoice.

- Ramp economics and discounting:
  - Month 1: 25% committed capacity, billed at 55% of full committed rate
  - Month 2: 50% committed capacity, billed at 65% of full committed rate
  - Month 3: 75% committed capacity, billed at 80% of full committed rate
  - Month 4 onward: 100% committed capacity at contracted rate
  - In addition: a 10% term discount for 12-month commit (applies to platform fee and committed capacity) or 18% for 24-month.

Rationale: This preserves revenue predictability while giving Industrial.ai a graded ramp and meaningful upfront concession (onboarding deposit + reduced ramp rates). It also allows Redwood to plan capacity and support during the onboarding load.

Other items
- We will populate your procurement template with line-item commercial fields by EOD tomorrow and attach a final SOW for legal review.
- Vivek confirmed we can implement the 25/50/75/100 ramp of reserved node pools in Private/VPC with automated scaling policies; 60-day delay on committed capacity could be accommodated as an exception but would require a larger onboarding deposit or higher month-1 billing.
- SOC 2 and SSO/KMS artifacts: Grace will share a zipped artifact set via secure link after I get procurement approval to share (PII/data-use check).

Next steps
1) Marissa to send populated procurement template + final MAP (by EOD 3/16).
2) Industrial.ai procurement to review and flag any legal redlines.
3) Commercials & SOW to legal for parallel review; sign when both sides agree.

If these terms look acceptable at a commercial level, we can lock dates and move to SOW prep.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RDW_Private_VPC_Licensing_Summary.pdf (pdf)]
